declarations.name: Code
declarations.doc:
Here we define a *Code* by an encdoder and a decoder. The encoder is a function that takes
strings (`List`s) of any length over an alphabet `A`, and returns strings over `I`;
the decoder takes `O` and gives back strings over `A`. The idea is that a channel
would map from strings of `I` to `O`. Important special cases are where `I=O` (the channel doesn't
change the symbol set), and `FixedLengthCode` where the output lengths only depend on input
lengths.
declarations.statement:
structure Code where
  encoder : List A → List I
  decoder : List O → List A

declarations.name: FixedLengthCode
declarations.doc:
A `FixedLengthCode` is a `Code` whose output lengths don't depend on the input content, only
the input length.
declarations.statement:
structure FixedLengthCode extends Code A I O where
  enc_length : ℕ → ℕ
  enc_maps_length : ∀ as, (encoder as).length = enc_length (as.length)
  dec_length : ℕ → ℕ
  dec_maps_length : ∀ is, (decoder is).length = dec_length (is.length)

declarations.name: DMChannel
declarations.doc:
Discrete Memoryless Channel. Each input symbol `I` has a corresponding
output distribution `Distribution O`, and this process is applied
independently on each symbol in the list.
declarations.statement:
structure DMChannel where
  symb_dist : I → ProbDistribution O

declarations.name: DMChannel.on_fin
declarations.doc: Apply a discrete memoryless channel to an n-character string.
declarations.statement: def on_fin (C : DMChannel I O) {n : ℕ} (is : Fin n → I) : ProbDistribution (Fin n → O)

declarations.name: DMChannel.on_list
declarations.doc: Apply a discrete memoryless channel to a list.
declarations.statement: def on_list (C : DMChannel I O) (is : List I) : ProbDistribution (Fin (is.length) → O)

modules.title: Distributions on finite sets
modules.doc:
We define the type `Distribution α` on a `Fintype α`. By restricting ourselves to distributoins on
finite types, a lot of notation and casts are greatly simplified.
This suffices for (most) finite-dimensional quantum theory.

declarations.name: ProbDistribution
declarations.doc:
We define our own (discrete) probability distribution notion here, instead
of using `PMF` from Mathlib, because that uses ENNReals everywhere to maintain compatibility
with `MeasureTheory.Measure`.

The probabilities internal to a Distribution are NNReals. This lets us more easily
write the statement that they sum to 1, since NNReals can be added. (Probabilities,
on their own, cannot.) But the FunLike instance gives `Prob` out, which carry the
information that they are all in the range [0,1].
declarations.statement: def ProbDistribution (α : Type u) [Fintype α] : Type u

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.mk'
declarations.doc:
Make a distribution, proving only that the values are nonnegative and that the
sum is 1. The fact that the values are at most 1 is derived as a consequence.
declarations.statement: def mk' (f : α → ℝ) (h₁ : ∀i, 0 ≤ f i) (hN : ∑ i, f i = 1) : ProbDistribution α

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.instFunLikeProb
declarations.statement: instance instFunLikeProb : FunLike (ProbDistribution α) α Prob

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.normalized
declarations.statement: lemma normalized (d : ProbDistribution α) : Finset.sum Finset.univ (fun i ↦ (d i : ℝ)) = 1

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.prob
declarations.statement: abbrev prob (d : ProbDistribution α)

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.fun_eq_val
declarations.statement: lemma fun_eq_val (d : ProbDistribution α) : d.val = d

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.funlike_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma funlike_apply (d : α → Prob) (h : _) (x : α) :
    DFunLike.coe (self := instFunLikeProb) ⟨d, h⟩ x = d x

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.ext
declarations.statement: lemma ext {p q : ProbDistribution α} (h : ∀ x, p x = q x) : p = q

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.nonempty
declarations.doc: A distribution provides a witness that d is nonempty.
declarations.statement: theorem nonempty (d : ProbDistribution α) : Nonempty α

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.constant
declarations.doc:
Make an constant distribution: supported on a single element. This is also called, variously, a
"One-point distribution", a "Degenerate distribution", a "Deterministic distribution", a
"Delta function", or a "Point mass distribution".
declarations.statement: def constant (x : α) : ProbDistribution α

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.constant_def
declarations.statement: lemma constant_def (x : α) : (constant x : α → Prob) = fun y ↦ if x = y then 1 else 0

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.constant_eq
declarations.statement: lemma constant_eq (x : α) : constant x y = if x = y then 1 else 0

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.constant_def'
declarations.statement: lemma constant_def' (x y : α) : (constant x : α → Prob) y = if x = y then 1 else 0

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.constant_of_exists_one
declarations.doc: If a distribution has an element with probability 1, the distribution has a constant.
declarations.statement:
theorem constant_of_exists_one {D : ProbDistribution α} {x : α} (h : D x = 1) :
    D = ProbDistribution.constant x

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.uniform
declarations.doc: Make an uniform distribution.
declarations.statement: def uniform [n : Nonempty α] : ProbDistribution α

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.uniform_def
declarations.statement: lemma uniform_def [Nonempty α] (y : α) : ((uniform y) : ℝ) = 1 / (Finset.univ.card (α := α))

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.prod
declarations.doc: Make a distribution on a product of two Fintypes.
declarations.statement: def prod (d1 : ProbDistribution α) (d2 : ProbDistribution β) : ProbDistribution (Prod α β)

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.prod_def
declarations.statement: lemma prod_def (x : α) (y : β) : prod d1 d2 ⟨x, y⟩ = (d1 x) * (d2 y)

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.extend_right
declarations.doc:
Given a distribution on α, extend it to a distribution on `Sum α β` by
giving it no support on `β`.
declarations.statement: def extend_right (d : ProbDistribution α) : ProbDistribution (α ⊕ β)

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.extend_left
declarations.doc:
Given a distribution on α, extend it to a distribution on `Sum β α` by
giving it no support on `β`.
declarations.statement: def extend_left (d : ProbDistribution α) : ProbDistribution (β ⊕ α)

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.instMixable
declarations.doc: Make a convex mixture of two distributions on the same set.
declarations.statement: instance instMixable : Mixable (α → ℝ) (ProbDistribution α)

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.relabel
declarations.doc:
Given a distribution on type α and an equivalence to type β, get the corresponding
distribution on type β.
declarations.statement: def relabel (d : ProbDistribution α) (σ : β ≃ α) : ProbDistribution β

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.congr
declarations.doc: ProbDistribution on α and β are equivalent for equivalent types α ≃ β.
declarations.statement: def congr (σ : α ≃ β) : ProbDistribution α ≃ ProbDistribution β

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.congr_apply
declarations.statement: lemma congr_apply (σ : α ≃ β) (d : ProbDistribution α) (j : β): (congr σ d) j = d (σ.symm j)

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.congr_symm_apply
declarations.doc: The inverse and congruence operations for distributions commute
declarations.statement:
theorem congr_symm_apply (σ : α ≃ β) :
    (ProbDistribution.congr σ).symm = ProbDistribution.congr σ.symm

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.coin
declarations.doc:
The distribution on Fin 2 corresponding to a coin with probability p.
Chance p of 1, 1-p of 0.
declarations.statement: def coin (p : Prob) : ProbDistribution (Fin 2)

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.coin_val_zero
declarations.statement: lemma coin_val_zero (p : Prob) : coin p 0 = p

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.coin_val_one
declarations.statement: lemma coin_val_one (p : Prob) : coin p 1 = 1 - p

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.fin_two_eq_coin
declarations.doc: Every distribution on two variable is some coin.
declarations.statement: theorem fin_two_eq_coin (d : ProbDistribution (Fin 2)) : d = coin (d 0)

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.coin_eq_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma coin_eq_iff (p : Prob) (f : ProbDistribution (Fin 2)) :
    ProbDistribution.coin p = f ↔ p = f 0

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.RandVar
declarations.doc:
A `T`-valued random variable over `α` is a map `var : α → T` along
with a probability distribution `distr : Distribution α`.
declarations.statement:
structure RandVar (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (T : Type*) where
  var : α → T
  distr : ProbDistribution α

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.instFunctor
declarations.statement: instance instFunctor : Functor (RandVar α)

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.instLawfulFunctor
declarations.statement: instance instLawfulFunctor : LawfulFunctor (RandVar α)

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.expect_val
declarations.doc:
`Distribution.exp_val` is the expectation value of a random variable `X`. Under the hood,
it is the "convex combination over a finite family" on the type `T`, afforded by
the `Mixable` instance, with the probability distribution of `X` as weights.
declarations.statement: def expect_val (X : RandVar α T) : T

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.expect_val_eq_mixable_mix
declarations.doc:
The expectation value of a random variable over `α = Fin 2` is the same as `Mixable.mix`
with probabiliy weight `X.distr 0`
declarations.statement:
theorem expect_val_eq_mixable_mix (d : ProbDistribution (Fin 2)) (x₁ x₂ : T) :
    expect_val ⟨![x₁, x₂], d⟩ = Mixable.mix (d 0) x₁ x₂

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.expect_val_constant
declarations.doc:
The expectation value of a random variable with constant probability distribution
`constant x` is its value at `x`
declarations.statement: theorem expect_val_constant (x : α) (f : α → T) : expect_val ⟨f, (constant x)⟩ = f x

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.zero_le_expect_val
declarations.doc: The expectation value of a nonnegative real random variable is also nonnegative
declarations.statement:
theorem zero_le_expect_val (d : ProbDistribution α) (f : α → ℝ) (hpos : 0 ≤ f) :
    0 ≤ expect_val ⟨f, d⟩

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.congrRandVar
declarations.doc: `T`-valued random variables on `α` and `β` are equivalent if `α ≃ β`
declarations.statement: def congrRandVar (σ : α ≃ β) : RandVar α T ≃ RandVar β T

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.map_congr_eq_congr_map
declarations.doc:
Given a `T`-valued random variable `X` over `α`, mapping over `T` commutes
with the equivalence over `α`
declarations.statement:
lemma map_congr_eq_congr_map {S : Type _} [Mixable U S] (f : T → S) (σ : α ≃ β) (X : RandVar α T) :
  f <$> congrRandVar σ X = congrRandVar σ (f <$> X)

declarations.name: ProbDistribution.expect_val_congr_eq_expect_val
declarations.doc: The expectation value is invariant under equivalence of random variables
declarations.statement:
theorem expect_val_congr_eq_expect_val (σ : α ≃ β) (X : RandVar α T) :
    expect_val (congrRandVar σ X) = expect_val X

modules.title: Shannon entropy
modules.doc:
Definitions and facts about the Shannon entropy function -x*ln(x), both on a single
variable and on a distribution.

There is significant overlap with `Real.negMulLog` and `Real.binEntropy` in Mathlib,
and probably these files could be combined in some form.

declarations.name: H₁
declarations.doc: The one-event entropy function, H₁(p) = -p*ln(p). Uses nits.
declarations.statement: def H₁ : Prob → ℝ

declarations.name: H₁_zero_eq_zero
declarations.doc: H₁ of 0 is zero.
declarations.statement: lemma H₁_zero_eq_zero : H₁ 0 = 0

declarations.name: H₁_one_eq_zero
declarations.doc: H₁ of 1 is zero.
declarations.statement: lemma H₁_one_eq_zero : H₁ 1 = 0

declarations.name: H₁_nonneg
declarations.doc: Entropy is nonnegative.
declarations.statement: theorem H₁_nonneg (p : Prob) : 0 ≤ H₁ p

declarations.name: H₁_le_1
declarations.doc: Entropy is less than 1.
declarations.statement: theorem H₁_le_1 (p : Prob) : H₁ p < 1

declarations.name: H₁_le_exp_m1
declarations.doc: Entropy is at most 1/e.
declarations.statement: theorem H₁_le_exp_m1 (p : Prob) : H₁ p ≤ Real.exp (-1)

declarations.name: H₁_concave
declarations.statement: lemma H₁_concave : ∀ (x y : Prob), ∀ (p : Prob), p[H₁ x ↔ H₁ y] ≤ H₁ (p[x ↔ y])

declarations.name: Hₛ
declarations.doc: The Shannon entropy of a discrete distribution, H(X) = ∑ H₁(p_x).
declarations.statement: def Hₛ (d : ProbDistribution α) : ℝ

declarations.name: Hₛ_eq_expect_val
declarations.doc:
Shannon entropy is the expected negative logarithm of the outcome probability.
Zero-probability outcomes contribute zero to the expectation.
declarations.statement:
lemma Hₛ_eq_expect_val (d : ProbDistribution α) :
    Hₛ d = ProbDistribution.expect_val ⟨fun x ↦ -Real.log (d x), d⟩

declarations.name: Hₛ_nonneg
declarations.doc: Shannon entropy of a distribution is nonnegative.
declarations.statement: theorem Hₛ_nonneg (d : ProbDistribution α) : 0 ≤ Hₛ d

declarations.name: Hₛ_concave
declarations.doc: Shannon entropy is concave under convex mixtures of distributions.
declarations.statement:
lemma Hₛ_concave (d₁ d₂ : ProbDistribution α) (p : Prob) :
    p[Hₛ d₁ ↔ Hₛ d₂] ≤ Hₛ (p[d₁ ↔ d₂])

declarations.name: Hₛ_le_log_d
declarations.doc: Shannon entropy of a distribution is at most ln d.
declarations.statement: theorem Hₛ_le_log_d (d : ProbDistribution α) : Hₛ d ≤ Real.log (Fintype.card α)

declarations.name: Hₛ_constant_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The shannon entropy of a constant variable is zero.
declarations.statement: theorem Hₛ_constant_eq_zero {i : α} : Hₛ (ProbDistribution.constant i) = 0

declarations.name: Hₛ_uniform
declarations.doc: Shannon entropy of a uniform distribution is ln d.
declarations.statement:
theorem Hₛ_uniform [Nonempty α] :
    Hₛ (ProbDistribution.uniform (α := α)) = Real.log (Finset.univ.card (α := α))

declarations.name: Hₛ_coin
declarations.doc: Shannon entropy of two-event distribution.
declarations.statement: theorem Hₛ_coin (p : Prob) : Hₛ (ProbDistribution.coin p) = Real.binEntropy p

declarations.name: Hₛ_eq_of_multiset_map_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma Hₛ_eq_of_multiset_map_eq (d₁ : ProbDistribution α) (d₂ : ProbDistribution β)
    (h : Multiset.map d₁.prob Finset.univ.val = Multiset.map d₂.prob Finset.univ.val) :
    Hₛ d₁ = Hₛ d₂

declarations.name: Real.negMulLog_strictMonoOn
declarations.statement: lemma negMulLog_strictMonoOn : StrictMonoOn Real.negMulLog (Set.Icc 0 (exp (-1)))

declarations.name: Real.negMulLog_strictAntiOn
declarations.statement: lemma negMulLog_strictAntiOn : StrictAntiOn Real.negMulLog (Set.Ici (exp (-1)))

declarations.name: Real.negMulLog_le_rexp_neg_one
declarations.statement: lemma negMulLog_le_rexp_neg_one {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 ≤ x) : negMulLog x ≤ exp (-1)

modules.title: Probabilities
modules.doc:
This defines a type `Prob`, which is simply any real number in the interval O to 1.
This then comes with additional statements such as its application to convex sets, and
it makes useful type alias for functions that only make sense on probabilities.

A significant application is in the `Mixable` typeclass, also in this file, which is a
general notion of convex combination that applies to types as opposed to sets;
elements are `Mixable.mix`ed using `Prob`s.

declarations.name: Prob
declarations.doc:
`Prob` is a real number in the interval [0,1]. Similar to NNReal in many definitions, but this
allows other nice things more 'safely' such as convex combination.
declarations.statement: def Prob : Type _
instance : Coe Prob ℝ

declarations.name: Prob.canLift
declarations.statement: instance canLift : CanLift ℝ Prob Subtype.val fun r => 0 ≤ r ∧ r ≤ 1

declarations.name: Prob.coe_zero
declarations.statement: lemma coe_zero : (0 : Prob).val = 0

declarations.name: Prob.coe_one
declarations.statement: lemma coe_one : (1 : Prob).val = 1

declarations.name: Prob.coe_mul
declarations.statement: lemma coe_mul (x y : Prob) : (x * y).val = x.val * y.val

declarations.name: Prob.coe_inf
declarations.statement: lemma coe_inf (x y : Prob) : (x ⊓ y).val = x.val ⊓ y.val

declarations.name: Prob.coe_sup
declarations.statement: lemma coe_sup (x y : Prob) : (x ⊔ y).val = x.val ⊔ y.val

declarations.name: Prob.instInhabited
declarations.statement: instance instInhabited : Inhabited Prob

declarations.name: Prob.instConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder
declarations.doc:
Override `ordConnectedSubsetConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder` (activated by `instInhabited`)
so that `ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder Prob` agrees definitionally with
`CompleteLinearOrder Prob`.

This seems fixed in Mathlib master.
declarations.statement:
instance (priority := high) instConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder :
    ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder Prob

declarations.name: Prob.zero_le_coe
declarations.statement: lemma zero_le_coe {p : Prob} : 0 ≤ (p : ℝ)

declarations.name: Prob.coe_le_one
declarations.statement: lemma coe_le_one {p : Prob} : (p : ℝ) ≤ 1

declarations.name: Prob.zero_le
declarations.statement: lemma zero_le {p : Prob} : 0 ≤ p

declarations.name: Prob.le_one
declarations.statement: lemma le_one {p : Prob} : p ≤ 1

declarations.name: Prob.mem_unitInterval_bounds
declarations.statement: lemma mem_unitInterval_bounds {x : ℝ} (h : x ∈ unitInterval) : 0 ≤ x ∧ x ≤ 1

declarations.name: Prob.mem_unitInterval_of_le
declarations.statement: lemma mem_unitInterval_of_le {x : ℝ} (h₀ : 0 ≤ x) (h₁ : x ≤ 1) : x ∈ unitInterval

declarations.name: Prob.ext
declarations.statement: protected lemma ext {n m : Prob} : (n : ℝ) = (m : ℝ) → n = m

declarations.name: Prob.ne_iff
declarations.statement: lemma ne_iff {x y : Prob} : (x : ℝ) ≠ (y : ℝ) ↔ x ≠ y

declarations.name: Prob.toReal_mul
declarations.statement: lemma toReal_mul (x y : Prob) : (x * y : Prob) = (x : ℝ) * (y : ℝ)

declarations.name: Prob.toNNReal
declarations.doc: Coercion `Prob → ℝ≥0`.
declarations.statement: def toNNReal : Prob → ℝ≥0

declarations.name: Prob.toNNReal_mk
declarations.statement: lemma toNNReal_mk : toNNReal { val := x, property := hx} = { val := x, property := hx.1 }
instance : Coe Prob ℝ≥0

declarations.name: Prob.canLiftNN
declarations.statement: instance canLiftNN : CanLift ℝ≥0 Prob toNNReal fun r => r ≤ 1

declarations.name: Prob.eq_iff_nnreal
declarations.statement: protected lemma eq_iff_nnreal (n m : Prob) : (n : ℝ≥0) = (m : ℝ≥0) ↔ n = m

declarations.name: Prob.toNNReal_zero
declarations.statement: lemma toNNReal_zero : (0 : Prob) = (0 : ℝ≥0)

declarations.name: Prob.toNNReal_one
declarations.statement: lemma toNNReal_one : (1 : Prob) = (1 : ℝ≥0)

declarations.name: Prob.ofNNReal_toNNReal
declarations.statement: lemma ofNNReal_toNNReal : ENNReal.ofNNReal (toNNReal p) = ENNReal.ofReal (p : ℝ)

declarations.name: Prob.NNReal.asProb
declarations.statement: def NNReal.asProb (p : ℝ≥0) (hp : p ≤ 1) : Prob

declarations.name: Prob.NNReal.asProb'
declarations.statement: def NNReal.asProb' (p : ℝ≥0) (hp : p.1 ≤ 1) : Prob

declarations.name: Prob.zero_lt_coe
declarations.statement: lemma zero_lt_coe {p : Prob} (hp : p ≠ 0) : (0 : ℝ) < p

declarations.name: Prob.instSub
declarations.doc:
Subtract a probability from another. Truncates to zero, so this is often not great
to work with, for the same reason that Nat subtraction is a pain. But, it lets you write
`1 - p`, which is sufficiently useful on its own that this seems worth having.
declarations.statement: instance instSub : Sub Prob

declarations.name: Prob.coe_sub
declarations.statement: lemma coe_sub (p q : Prob) : (p - q : Prob)  = (p.val - q.val) ⊔ (0 : ℝ)

declarations.name: Prob.coe_one_minus
declarations.statement: lemma coe_one_minus (p : Prob) : (1 - p : Prob) = 1 - (p : ℝ)

declarations.name: Prob.add_one_minus
declarations.statement: lemma add_one_minus (p : Prob) : p.val + (1 - p).val = 1

declarations.name: Prob.one_minus_inv
declarations.statement: lemma one_minus_inv (p : Prob) : 1 - (1 - p) = p

declarations.name: Prob.coe_iInf
declarations.statement: lemma coe_iInf {ι : Type*} [Nonempty ι] (f : ι → Prob) : ↑(⨅ t, f t) = (⨅ t, f t : ℝ)

declarations.name: Prob.top_eq_one
declarations.statement: lemma top_eq_one : (⊤ : Prob) = 1

declarations.name: Prob.sub_zero
declarations.statement: lemma sub_zero (p : Prob) : p - 0 = p

declarations.name: Prob.toNNReal_Continuous
declarations.statement: lemma toNNReal_Continuous : Continuous Prob.toNNReal

declarations.name: Prob.mul_eq_one_iff
declarations.statement: lemma mul_eq_one_iff (p q : Prob) : p * q = 1 ↔ p = 1 ∧ q = 1

declarations.name: Mixable
declarations.doc:
A `Mixable T` typeclass instance gives a compact way of talking about the
action of probabilities for forming linear combinations in convex spaces.
The notation `p [ x₁ ↔ x₂ ]` means to take a convex
combination, equal to `x₁` if `p=1` and to `x₂` if `p=0`.

Mixable is defined by an "underlying" data type `U` with addition and scalar
multiplication, and a bijection between the `T` and a convex set of `U`.
For instance, in `Mixable (Distribution (Fin n))`, `U` is `n`-element vectors
(which form the probability simplex, degenerate in one dimension). For
`QuantumInfo.States.Mixed.MState` density matrices in quantum mechanics, which are
PSD matrices of trace 1, `U` is the underlying matrix.

Why not just stick with existing notions of `Convex`? `Convex` requires that
the type already forms an `AddCommMonoid` and `Module ℝ`. But many types, such as `Distribution`,
are not: there is no good notion of "multiplying a probability distribution by 0.3" to get another
distribution. We can coerce the distribution nto, say, a vector or a function, but then we are not
doing arithmetic with distributions. Accordingly, the expression `0.3 * distA + 0.7 * distB`
cannot represent a distribution on its own.
declarations.statement:
class Mixable (U : outParam (Type u)) (T : Type v) [AddCommMonoid U] [Module ℝ U] where
  /-- Getter for the underlying data -/
  to_U : T → U
  /-- Proof that this getter is injective -/
  to_U_inj : ∀ {T₁ T₂}, to_U T₁ = to_U T₂ → T₁ = T₂
  /-- Proof that this image is convex -/
  convex : Convex ℝ (Set.range to_U)
  /-- Function to get a T from a proof that U is in the set. -/
  mkT : {u : U} → (∃ t, to_U t = u) → { t : T // to_U t = u }

declarations.name: Mixable.mix_ab
declarations.statement: def mix_ab [inst : Mixable U T] {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hb : 0 ≤ b) (hab : a + b = 1) (x₁ x₂ : T) : T

declarations.name: Mixable.mix
declarations.doc:
`Mixable.mix` represents the notion of "convex combination" on the type `T`, afforded by the
`Mixable` instance. It takes a `Prob`, that is, a `Real` between 0 and 1. For working directly
with a Real, use `mix_ab`.
declarations.statement: def mix [inst : Mixable U T] (p : Prob) (x₁ x₂ : T) : T

declarations.name: Mixable.to_U_of_mkT
declarations.statement: lemma to_U_of_mkT [inst : Mixable U T] (u : U) {h} : inst.to_U (mkT (u := u) h).1 = u

declarations.name: Mixable.mix_zero
declarations.statement: lemma mix_zero [inst : Mixable U T] (x₁ x₂ : T) : (0 : Prob) [ x₁ ↔ x₂ : inst] = x₂

declarations.name: Mixable.mix_one
declarations.statement: lemma mix_one [inst : Mixable U T] (x₁ x₂ : T) : (1 : Prob) [ x₁ ↔ x₂ : inst] = x₁

declarations.name: Mixable.instUniv
declarations.doc: When T is the whole space, and T is a suitable vector space over ℝ, we get a Mixable instance.
declarations.statement: instance instUniv [AddCommMonoid T] [Module ℝ T] : Mixable T T

declarations.name: Mixable.mkT_instUniv
declarations.statement:
lemma mkT_instUniv [AddCommMonoid T] [Module ℝ T] {t : T} (h : ∃ t', to_U t' = t) :
    instUniv.mkT h = ⟨t, rfl⟩

declarations.name: Mixable.to_U_instUniv
declarations.statement: lemma to_U_instUniv [AddCommMonoid T] [Module ℝ T] {t : T} : instUniv.to_U t = t

declarations.name: Mixable.instPi.lem_1
declarations.statement:
lemma instPi.lem_1 {D : Type*} {T U : D → Type*} [∀i, AddCommMonoid (U i)] [∀ i, Module ℝ (U i)]
    [inst : ∀i, Mixable (U i) (T i)]
    {u : (i : D) → U i} (h : ∃ (t : (i : D) → T i), (fun d => to_U (t d)) = u) (d : D) :
    ∃ (t : T d), to_U t = u d

declarations.name: Mixable.instPi
declarations.doc: Mixable instance on Pi types.
declarations.statement: instance instPi : Mixable ((i:D) → U i) ((i:D) → T i)

declarations.name: Mixable.val_mkT_instPi
declarations.statement:
lemma val_mkT_instPi (D : Type*) [inst : Mixable U T] {u : D → U} (h : ∃ t, to_U t = u) :
    (instPi.mkT h).val = fun d ↦ (inst.mkT (instPi.lem_1 h d)).val

declarations.name: Mixable.to_U_instPi
declarations.statement:
lemma to_U_instPi (D : Type*) [inst : Mixable U T] {t : D → T} :
    (instPi).to_U t = fun d ↦ inst.to_U (t d)

declarations.name: Mixable.instSubtype
declarations.doc:
Mixable instances on subtypes (of other mixable types), assuming that they
have the correct closure properties.

declarations.name: Prob.instMixable
declarations.doc: Probabilities `Prob` themselves are convex.
declarations.statement: instance instMixable : Mixable ℝ Prob

declarations.name: Prob.to_U_mixable
declarations.statement: lemma to_U_mixable [AddCommMonoid T] [SMul ℝ T] (t : Prob) : instMixable.to_U t = t.val

declarations.name: Prob.mkT_mixable
declarations.statement:
lemma mkT_mixable (u : ℝ) (h : ∃ t : Prob, Mixable.to_U t = u) : Mixable.mkT h =
    ⟨⟨u,Exists.casesOn h fun t ht ↦ ht ▸ t.2⟩, rfl⟩

declarations.name: Prob.mix
declarations.doc:
`Prob.mix` is an alias of `Mixable.mix` so it can be accessed from a probability with
dot notation, e.g. `p.mix x y`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev mix [AddCommMonoid U] [Module ℝ U] [inst : Mixable U T]
    (p : Prob) (x₁ x₂ : T)

declarations.name: Prob.negLog
declarations.doc:
Map a probability [0,1] to [0,+∞] with -log p. Special case that 0 maps to +∞ (not 0, as
Real.log does). This makes it strictly antitone.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def negLog : Prob → ENNReal

declarations.name: Prob.negLog_strictAnti
declarations.doc: Smaller probabilities have strictly greater negative logarithms, including at zero.
declarations.statement: lemma negLog_strictAnti : StrictAnti negLog

declarations.name: Prob.negLog_Antitone
declarations.statement: lemma negLog_Antitone : Antitone negLog

declarations.name: Prob.negLog_zero
declarations.statement: lemma negLog_zero : —log (0 : Prob) = ⊤

declarations.name: Prob.negLog_one
declarations.statement: lemma negLog_one : —log 1 = 0

declarations.name: Prob.negLog_eq_top_iff
declarations.statement: lemma negLog_eq_top_iff {p : Prob} : —log p = ⊤ ↔ p = 0

declarations.name: Prob.negLog_pos_ENNReal
declarations.statement:
lemma negLog_pos_ENNReal {p : Prob} (hp : p ≠ 0) : —log p = .ofNNReal ⟨-Real.log p,
    Left.nonneg_neg_iff.mpr (Real.log_nonpos p.2.1 p.2.2)⟩

declarations.name: Prob.negLog_pos_Real
declarations.statement: lemma negLog_pos_Real {p : Prob} : (—log p).toReal = -Real.log p

declarations.name: Prob.le_negLog_of_le_exp
declarations.statement: lemma le_negLog_of_le_exp {p : Prob} {x : ℝ} (h : p ≤ Real.exp (-x)) : ENNReal.ofReal x ≤ —log p

declarations.name: Prob.negLog_ne_top
declarations.statement: lemma negLog_ne_top {p : Prob} (hp : 0 < p.val) : —log p ≠ ∞

declarations.name: Prob.negLog_eq_neg_ENNReal_log
declarations.statement: lemma negLog_eq_neg_ENNReal_log (p : Prob) : —log p = -ENNReal.log p

declarations.name: Prob.negLog_eq_ofReal_neg_log
declarations.statement:
lemma negLog_eq_ofReal_neg_log {p : Prob} (hp : 0 < p) :
    ENNReal.ofReal (-Real.log p) = —log p

declarations.name: Prob.negLog_surjective
declarations.doc: Every extended nonnegative value is the negative logarithm of a probability.
declarations.statement: lemma negLog_surjective : Function.Surjective negLog

declarations.name: Prob.negLogOrderIso
declarations.doc:
The negative logarithm identifies probabilities with extended nonnegative values in reverse
order, sending zero to infinity and one to zero.
declarations.statement: def negLogOrderIso : Prob ≃o ENNRealᵒᵈ

declarations.name: Prob.negLogOrderIso_apply
declarations.statement: lemma negLogOrderIso_apply (p : Prob) : negLogOrderIso p = OrderDual.toDual (negLog p)

declarations.name: Prob.zero_lt_negLog
declarations.statement: lemma zero_lt_negLog {p : Prob} : 0 < —log p ↔ p ≠ 1

declarations.name: Prob.Continuous_negLog
declarations.statement: lemma Continuous_negLog : Continuous negLog
